title: Sir Simonds D'Ewes, cipher log of his son Clopton's convulsion fits, 1635-36, BL Harley MS 286 f. 61 (DECODE R7759)

documents.shelfmark: BL Harley MS 286 f. 61 (DECODE R7759; the BL online catalogue lists the paper under Harley MS 289 f. 61r)

plaintext.source: No decipherment found. The Autobiography (Halliwell 1845, ii 143-144) paraphrases the content in English (44 fits, 3 Apr 1635 - 4 Mar 1636) but gives no Latin text.

transcription.source: DECODE full-resolution JPEG (7230 x 9965 px), line crops; harley286/transcription.tsv, harley286/cipher.txt
transcription.notes: 281 cipher words measured (cipher.txt, the glyph column); 1112 signs with --letters. transcription.tsv counts 287 word slots because it includes the struck words and the estimated words of the trimmed last line; the read bar is computed on those 287. Only heading 1635 and margin dates are clear.

system.summary: D'Ewes's private invented alphabet: simple substitution of Latin, one sign per letter (p and g share a sign), numerals written with the letter signs, words divided.
system.sibling_key: none; same-volume key records R7753-R7758 are other material, not used
system.notes: Several signs are Latin letters used for other values (r=i, x=r, c=e, S=u/v, X=d, o=o); ʒ is initial I; y = ii in Maii.

prior_solution.where: No reading of this slip found. UMN 1915 thesis deciphered D'Ewes's 1622-24 diary (Harley 481) without printing a key; Bourcier 1974 and Notestein 1923 mention his cipher. The Autobiography paraphrases the content only.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: DECODE login cookie, Claude Code setup, posed the target from the catalogue entry. No target-specific intervention.

solution.what: Fetched the two page images of R7759 from DECODE with the session cookie; p2 is verso show-through only.
BL online catalogue search: 'a short paper written by Sir Simonds D'Ewes, in his cipher' (listed under Harley 289 f. 61r).
Looked for a printed key to D'Ewes's alphabet: UMN 1915 thesis on the Harley 481 diary, Notestein 1923.
Hand crib on recurring words: 'plena luna', 'convulsio(nem)', 'difficil-'; with Latin month names and numerals this gave most of the alphabet.

Weekdays checked against the Julian calendar (3 Apr 1635 Friday, 23 Apr Thursday, 23 May Saturday: die Veneris / Iovis / Saturni all match) and moon phases (23 Apr full, 17/19 Jul full, 2 Aug new, 18 Aug full match; 25 May 'plena luna' and 12 Jun 'decrescente' do not, numerals confirmed at 3x: writer's slips).
Autobiography and Correspondence (Halliwell 1845, ii 143-144): 44 convulsion fits of Clopton D'Ewes from 3 April 1635 to 4 March following; confirms the first line's date.
Subagent full transcription and reading pass 1 over 30 line crops.
Pass 2 on re-crops at 3x: meos, amplexus, incidebat, tres, sperabam, convul-sum confirmed letter by letter; 277 of 287 words read.

outcome.fraction_read_source: harley286/transcription.tsv, cipher words (unread and total columns): 277/287; 12 further words doubtful

gaps.item: line 30, the last line, trimmed under the mount (about 6 words)
gaps.detail: only '...am nonam' visible; the edge is under the guard
cramped at the edge; 'postea' does not fit the signs
faint cramped ink; septima, pede, nativo in the same lines doubtful

outcome.notes: Every line of the log reads except the trimmed foot; running count 'huc usque xxxii' in the margin. Dates are Julian.
